messages.text: There's a comment on PR #101, have a look
I’ll read the new comment on PR #101 and check it against the current changes.

The [reviewer’s comment](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/101#issuecomment-6419397508) asks for a Fatras cross-check using Gaussian-smeared measurements with widths measured over all cluster sizes.

Yes, the current baseline uses cluster-size-dependent errors from the independent Fatras training sample, applied after geometric clustering. I’ll add the smeared comparison so we can check how much the geometric digitization contributes to the pull shapes.

I’ll pool all cluster sizes within each ACTS volume and measured coordinate to set the Gaussian widths, using the existing independent training sample. The Spack preflight still warns about changed setup fingerprints; I’ll verify the existing isolated runtime before running the cross-check.

The pooled widths are ready: they use all 699,273 training measurements across 52 volumes and 90 measured coordinates. The new Gaussian configuration will use those same widths for both the random shifts and fitted measurement covariance. SoftEng is preparing a native pilot to verify this.

The native Gaussian pilot is running. One detail matters for interpretation: ACTS discards smeared positions that fall outside the sensor bounds. I’ll retain those losses and check measurement residuals as well as track pulls, since Gaussian measurement errors alone don’t guarantee Gaussian track pulls.

The 100-event pilot passed: all tracks fitted, both measurement dimensions were correct, and every written measurement variance matched the frozen Gaussian width squared. The three 20,000-event Fatras samples at 1, 10, and 100 GeV are now starting at one fixed source revision.
